files.document_title: Proposed Licking County Pipeline, project map dated 2026-03-26, from The Energy Cooperative (attached to the oilandgaswatch record)
files.what_it_shows: A one-page aerial-photo map of the proposed Licking County Pipeline in two colored phases. Phase 1 (blue) runs from near New Albany, south of the New Albany industrial area, east along State Route 161 past Alexandria to near Granville, then turns south to near State Route 16. Phase 2 (orange) continues east then south through the Heath and Hebron area and ends just north of US 40 east of Hebron. The map has a scale bar and a north arrow. The verifier could not extract text because the PDF is an image.
landmarks: Franklin County and Licking County line
Licking County and Fairfield County line

files.document_title: Map on The Energy Cooperative Licking County Pipeline project page, updated May 2026
files.what_it_shows: A newer web map from the cooperative page. A wide blue corridor band covers the Phase 2 area, running from State Route 161 near Granville south to near State Route 37 and then southeast to the Hebron area, and ends at a point labeled EGTS near National Road. A thin dashed blue line with dots follows State Route 161 from near New Albany east to a point labeled TCE near Granville. The corridor band is wide, so it shows the study area and not the final centerline. The labels TCE and EGTS are not spelled out on the map.

Stopped there because the March map is legible with more than four named landmarks; no Ohio Power Siting Board search was run for this row
notes: The March 2026 map is the better route map: it shows a single drawn line in two phases with a scale bar. The May 2026 web map shows Phase 2 only as a wide study corridor and adds the western Phase 1 line along State Route 161. The two maps agree on the general path. Phase 1 ends near State Route 16 and Phase 2 ends at the EGTS point south of Heath near National Road. The map shows the line within Licking County. Its length was not measured here. EGTS is probably Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, but the map does not say so. The first URL fails the text check only because the PDF is an image.
